content.text: I now have enough to write the two-file review preamble.

groups.overview: The Claude Bridge launch form previously accepted only images; this widens it to anything Claude Code's Read tool can open (PDFs, any UTF-8 text file) plus Office documents stored raw for Claude to work out itself. The one decision shaping the change is extension-first type resolution shared verbatim between server and browser — because the browser's own File.type lies for exactly these formats (empty for .md, application/vnd.ms-excel for .csv, video/mp2t for .ts), MIME is only a fallback for filenameless pastes. Scope was deliberately narrowed mid-review: an uploads-sweep for orphaned directories and a request-body size cap were cut back out to keep the PR to the attachment path itself.

groups.title: 1. server.mjs — attachment typing, storage and the /run wiring
groups.why: This is where the actual decision lives: how a file's type is decided, how it's validated and written to disk, and how the launched prompt is told where it landed. Everything else in the PR (the README, the browser-side mirror of these same rules) exists to describe or duplicate this logic.

files.preamble: Widens attachment handling from images-only to PDFs, Office docs, and arbitrary UTF-8 text. The core decision is the ATTACH_BY_EXT/ATTACH_BY_MIME table: extension resolves the type first, with MIME as a fallback only for filenameless pastes (a screenshot), because browsers misreport .md, .csv and .ts via File.type. saveAttachments() validates and decodes the base64 data URL, sniffs unrecognised extensions for UTF-8 text via looksLikeText(), and writes each file under a per-session uploads dir outside the repo so it never shows up in git status. The /run handler wires this in: it rejects the old `images` field with an explicit error, caps attachment count/size, and appends attachmentPromptBlock()'s file paths to the prompt so claude can open them by path — deliberately without a recipe for opening .docx, since that's claude's problem to solve with the tools it has. The same ATTACH_KINDS/ATTACH_MIME_KINDS tables are serialized into the inline browser script (search for ATTACH_KINDS_JSON) so client-side validation can never drift from the server's rules.

groups.title: 2. README.md — documents the new accepted formats and the type rule
groups.why: Explains the extension-first ordering and the accepted formats to a human operator, so it's read after the code that implements the rule it describes.

files.preamble: Updates the 'Form' section to describe the widened attachment support: images, PDFs, any UTF-8 text file, and Office docs (stored raw, with claude working out how to open them since nothing on the box converts them). Documents the extension-first/MIME-fallback type rule and why it exists, and notes the `/run` payload field was renamed from `images` to `attachments` with no back-compat alias.
